A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SHAP zero study and provide readable main text, Methods proofs, Tables S1–S6, and Figures S1–S4. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Fourier-sketch accuracy, attribution comparisons, runtimes, and biological case studies for TIGER and inDelphi, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and supplementary results and additionally reports two sketch-fit R² values.

M1.justification: The sparse Fourier sketch, query-dependent phase shift, Fourier-to-Möbius conversion, and SHAP/Faith-Shap computations are retained. Expanded notation and explanations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same TIGER guide-efficiency and inDelphi DNA-repair tasks, using the same 26-position and 40-position sequence settings. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain linear and pairwise models, KernelSHAP, SHAP-IQ, and FastSHAP, with DeepSHAP evaluated only on TIGER. Supplementary comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2's Introduction newly describes the 1,038 TIGER explanation sequences as training data, whereas both Methods sections specify held-out sequences. This changes the reported split description but introduces an inconsistency rather than establishing a rerun. Methods retains the evaluation budgets, metrics, and main sample counts.

E4.justification: The seed-region localization, attribution-overlap analyses, and microhomology case studies are retained, including Figures S1–S2 and Table S6. No new ablation, robustness test, or analytical question is introduced.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices and repeat/seed information are unchanged. Both versions report point estimates without adding confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Methods newly reports Fourier-sketch R² values of 0.55 for TIGER and 0.82 for inDelphi. Figure S4b revises SHAP zero's plotted runtime from approximately 210,000 to 320,000 seconds, while FastSHAP remains unchanged. Figures 2–3 and Tables S1–S6 retain their results.

T1.justification: The assumptions, Fourier–Möbius–SHAP formulas, theorem conclusions, and complexity derivations are retained. Added shifted-query identities and explicit support-index notation restate existing centering and marginalization steps rather than introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the exhaustive claim of recovering all microhomologous motifs to almost all predictive motifs, and the Introduction drops all-order from its empirical speedup claim. The three principal contributions and amortized-speedup claim remain.

C2.justification: Results adds an interpretation of SHAP signs in terms of average nucleotide-substitution effects. Methods newly notes that a direct Fourier-to-SHAP mapping might bypass the Möbius transform and explains retaining that connection. Existing biological interpretations and marginalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: Captions newly identify a Source Data file for Figures 2–3 and S1–S4. Existing GitHub and figshare access information, hardware disclosure, and implementation parameters are retained; the addition concerns access documentation.

R1.justification: The same 43 cited works are retained after matching reordered references and added arXiv identifiers. Positioning relative to sparse Fourier methods, Möbius transforms, and competing explainers is substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and selected Introduction and Methods passages are rewritten; notation is clarified, experimental subheadings are renamed, and author/contribution text is updated. The overall section sequence and most exposition are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 updates encoding and query-centered labels, and Figure S4b changes its runtime scale. Captions gain Source Data statements and change the stated TIGER display subsample from 40 to 50 in Figures 2c and S3a, although those plots are identical. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: Clearer query-centering and marginalization exposition, a qualified motif-recovery claim, and newly reported sketch-fit R² values provide limited improvements in clarity and reporting. The revised Figure S4b runtime also aligns with the inDelphi cost already reported around Figure 3. These benefits outweigh the new training-versus-held-out wording inconsistency, which weakens protocol clarity.
